Definitely to be placed INSIDE the "MY K CUP" filter basket. Without this filter I could put in a little more ground coffee in the mesh basket but the resulting residue was prohibitive. With this filter INSIDE the wire mesh basket I can still make one large mug plus an immediate second run on the same coffee for an addition medium or small cup (both cups combined into a thermal carafe). The taste is way bold enough for me and without the goop the mesh basket lets through! I fill the basket with this filter tucked inside to the top with coffee; there are a few drops of overrun on the second run, not significant. It's cost effective, works OK, and I can use my fresh ground Starbucks French Roast too! Just make sure the filter overlaps the top of the mesh filter basket when tucked inside to allow the My K Cup lid to hold it in place during brewing. Be patient and experiment a little until things are to your taste and satisfaction. It takes patience but the pure taste resulting from this filter trapping residue the wire mesh basket allows to pass makes it worth the time and effort! I am an Amazon seller, and send my products to their distribution centers for order fulfillment. This is a great sealer for sealing my products (mostly apparel), to keep the dust out. Currently I am using 2 mil bags, which are pretty durable, and you can also use poly tubing. The 16" width is long in comparison to others, but we sell corsets, dresses and other items which require a wider, 15" bag. It works just as well when sealing smaller width bags.

The sealer itself is pretty easy to use. I like the all-metal housing of this brand, versus the cheap plastic housing some others brands have. Because it has a metal housing, it has some "heft", and will not bounce around when quickly using it when sealing, and won't go flying across the table if you bump it. Overall, a nice product and a decent value.

Note: This will hermetically seal the bag completely, making it airtight. If you are selling apparel or similar items that might have a risk of damage from moisture, you might want to add a dessicant (i.e. a silica gel pack), to help absorb any moisture, if you are packing and sealing products in a humid environment. I use 1-gram silica gel packs, and you can find them on Amazon. The alternative is to punch a small hole in the corner of the sealed bag, so the item can "breathe," but then you risk warehouse dust making its way in.

This sealer is easy to use and fairly light weight. It comes with an extra heating element wire and heat resistant cloth. After experimenting with the heat dial, I found just below the half point is good for quick sealing of 75 gauge CF polyolefin shrink film.

The only caution I have with this, and it is minor, is it comes in a box with styrofoam end pieces that leave bits of foam all over when you remove it from the packaging.

Firstly, am not sure if I’ve previously written a review for this sealer. If so, I’m certain it was 5 stars!! We have this 16” sealer as well as two 8” sealers, and seems we’re grabbing one most every day. One nice thing that many folks may not have thought of is, these sealers will seal potato chip bags! Why would you want to? Well, for us, trash food scraps can be put in empty food bags (such as from chips) and sealed, keeping any odor locked inside.

We have a new litter of kittens and there was some food that sat out too long and I didn’t want to trust. So found a chip bag, dumped the old kitten chow in (water-soaked dry food mixed with canned paté) and sealed it up. …Or at least that was the plan.

We’ve had this sealer for 3 years and I’ve never had a problem. This time, I ended up cutting my finger on a piece of metal left over from the manufacturing process. On the bottom are two oblong holes. Each hole had excess metal that was not removed. Well, guess my tough-as-leather skin is no more, cause I got a cut. First couple of days went well but today is day 3 and it’s quite painful.

To remedy the problem, I took a pair of needle nose pliers and, using the rounded nose, formed the metal fragments up into the sealer housing. Now the unit will be safe for anyone to handle….even me! LOL

As mentioned, we have this 16” sealer as well as two smaller 8” sealers. Other than this issue, can’t say enough good about them. Wonderful tools. J
